newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, new deals firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, new deals firm.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond secondary prices ended flat Wednesday, overshadowed by a brisk new issue market that saw what one analyst called "firm" pricing on several large deals.
"Nothing is going on," one trader said, pointing to secondary market activity.

While primary market action -- including a $700 million Puerto Rico sale -- grabbed much of the focus, the trader said he was having little luck getting retail to bite in either market. Individual investors apparently find current price levels too expensive, he said.

"I'm not even getting retail interest in the primary," he said. "I can't get interest in anything, and I've taken some things in the secondary that in the past we've done a real good job on retail, and we're literally just nickel and diming bonds right now."

In the primary market, Lehman Brothers repriced $700 million Commonwealth of Puerto Rico bonds, trimming the top yield to 5.81 percent from 5.85 percent in 2026. Lehman, however, raised some yields in the early portion of the loan by 15 basis points.

"I thought it was good pricing, good, strong pricing," one analyst said of Puerto Rico's deal. While the analyst didn't focus on a $435 million Alaska Housing Finance Corp deal, primary market pricing overall was "essentially firm," he said.
Lehman Brothers also repriced the Alaska deal, cutting the 2017 maturity on the capital appreciation bond portion to 6.15 percent from 6.20 percent.
On the competitive side, Prudential Securities Inc said it won $215 million New York State general obligation bonds at a true interest cost of 5.34698 percent.

New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall said syndicates led by Lehman Brothers and Morgan Stanley & Co also submitted bids, with true interest costs of 5.34717 percent and 5.35779 percent, respectively. Proceeds will be used for a variety of state capital programs under various bond act authorizations, including clean water and infrastructure projects. In addition, $83 million of bond proceeds will be used to redeem outstanding bond anticipation notes.
Goldman Sachs & Co won $200 million Massachusetts GOs at a true interest cost of 4.98 percent. Underwriters declared the account closed by mid-afternoon.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed down 9/32 at 113-14/32. The June T-bond contract closed down 11/32 at 109-21/32. The MOB spread was 121 ticks.
In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 11/32 at 96-24/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
